newsitem.title: USA: Pat Buchanan takes CNN job.
newsitem.headline: Pat Buchanan takes CNN job.

text.p: Saying he has put his political ambitions aside, onetime Republican presidential contender Pat Buchanan announced Wednesday he has taken his old job back as a conservative commentator on CNN.

"The Gingrich-Clinton detente does not extend to 'Crossfire,'" Buchanan said in a telephone news conference to announce his return to "Crossfire," the combative liberal-conservative dialogue programme he help start almost 15 years ago and left in 1995 so he could run for president.
After beating Sen. Bob Dole in the 1996 Republican presidential primary in New Hampshire, Buchanan's conservative crusade faded and eventually he conceded he could not win the nomination.
Buchanan insisted he was just a journalist these days -- at least for the forseeable future.

"'Crossfire' is an excellent launching pad for the presidency," he joked, quickly adding, "Journalism is what I do. It is what I have made a living doing for the past 30 years. If I do an effective job, the grassroots will rise."
He said he saw himself doing only journalism. "Political activity has ended for me," he said. But he added he has not foreclosed anything in the future.
CNN Vice President Rick Davis, the executive producer of "Crossfire," said Buchanan would return March 3 and particpate in the programs' celebrations of its 15th anniversary in June.
